title: Shortest Heater Reach
statement:
Houses and heaters stand on a straight street. houses[i] and heaters[j] are their positions. Every heater has the same reach r: it warms every house at distance r or less.

Return the smallest whole-number reach r such that every house is warmed by at least one heater. Neither list is sorted, and several houses or heaters may share a position.

examples.why: One heater must reach both ends: the house at 9 is 5 away, the house at 1 is 3 away. The farther one decides.
Each house uses its nearest heater: 2 → 1 (1 away), 10 → 12 (2 away), 11 → 12 (1 away). The input is unsorted, so sort before searching.
Every house stands on a heater, so no reach is needed at all.

hints: The reach must cover the worst-off house. For a single house, what is the smallest reach that warms it?
A house needs exactly its distance to the nearest heater. The answer is the maximum of that over all houses.
Sort the heaters. For each house, binary search for the first heater at or after it; the nearest heater is that one or the one just before it.

explain.intuition:
A reach of r warms a house exactly when some heater is within r of it, so each house on its own needs the distance to its nearest heater. All heaters share one reach, so the answer is the largest of these per-house needs.

The only real work is finding each house's nearest heater fast. Once heaters are sorted, the nearest one is next to where the house would be inserted: the first heater at or to the right of it, or the one just before. Binary search finds that slot in O(log m). It is like snapping a dragged element to the nearest gridline.
steps: For each house, binary search for the first index i with heaters[i] ≥ house.
Its nearest distance is the smaller of heaters[i] − house (if i < m) and house − heaters[i − 1] (if i > 0).
Return the largest nearest distance over all houses.
pitfalls: Binary searching on unsorted heaters. Nothing says the input is sorted.
Checking only the heater on one side. The nearest heater can be to the left or to the right of the house.
Taking the minimum over houses instead of the maximum. The reach must cover the house that is worst off.

solutions.title: Nearest heater by scanning
solutions.idea: For every house, check every heater and keep the closest distance. The answer is the largest of those.

solutions.title: Sort heaters, binary search per house
solutions.idea: The nearest heater is on one side of the house's insertion point in the sorted heater list.

solutions.title: Sort both, walk with two pointers
solutions.idea: With houses sorted too, a house's nearest heater never lies left of the previous house's nearest heater, so one pointer only moves forward.
solutions.time: O(n log n + m log m)

followups: You may place k heaters anywhere instead. What is the smallest reach now? (Binary search on the answer plus a greedy check.)
Heaters have different reaches. Check whether every house is warm.
